item.title: Eventual Exactness and Rigidity for Abelian Covers of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.22388v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For a group $G$, let $a(G)$ denote the minimum number of abelian subgroups covering $G$, and let $\omega(G)$ be the maximum size of a pairwise noncommuting set. We prove the exact formula $\sup_{\omega(G)\leq n}a(G)=2^{\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor}+1$ for every $n\geq 63$. Equality holds precisely for groups with derived subgroup of order two and binary symplectic central quotient of dimension $2\lfloor(n-1)/2\rfloor$. The proof combines centralizer descent with a structural separation of nonscalar alternating commutator maps.
item.dc:creator: Guillaume Lecomte

item.title: Failure of direct finiteness for group algebras in every odd characteristic
item.description: arXiv:2610.22536v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For every odd prime $p$, we construct a finitely presented group $G_p$ and elements $a,b,c\in\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$ such that $ab=1$, $ac=0$, and $c\ne0$. Thus $\mathbb{F}_p[G_p]$, and the group algebra over every field of characteristic $p$, fails to be directly finite. The construction combines a single exceptional self-product pair with signed bipartite cancellation. New integer matching data realize the exceptional self-intersection while retaining a strict squared-word decay estimate. We verify the adaptations needed for the earlier bounded-path and planar-localization arguments. A minimal disk picture protects the identity coefficient of $c$, so the proof does not require torsion-freeness.
item.dc:creator: Elena I. Bunina, Winston Lee, Alexei Miasnikov, Kyrylo Muliarchyk

item.title: The Diophantine Problem in Wreath Products of Groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.22719v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the Diophantine problem in restricted wreath products of groups. Write $G=B\wr H$, where $B$ is the passive factor and $H$ is the active factor. The main results demonstrate that in a wide class of wreath products $G$, the Diophantine problem is undecidable. First, we show that if both factors are indicable, then $G$ has a retract isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}\wr\mathbb{Z}$ and therefore has undecidable Diophantine problem. Then, we show that for any groups $B$ and $H$, the Diophantine problems in $B$ and $H$ are polynomial time reducible to the Diophantine problem in $G$. Finally, we combine e-definability with retractions in order to prove that the Diophantine problem in $G$ is undecidable whenever $B$ is an infinite finitely generated abelian group and $H$ is a finitely generated group containing an infinite e-definable finitely generated abelian subgroup $A$.
item.dc:creator: Michael Catli, Alexei Myasnikov

item.title: Comparing word probabilities in finite groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23100v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We use results from extremal graph theory and analysis to compare word probabilities in finite groups. In particular, we show that the probability of satisfying the 2-Engel word admits a positive lower bound in terms of the probability that an element has order dividing 3. More generally, using a group removal lemma, we obtain analogous bounds for $x^m$-good words.
item.dc:creator: Lorenzo Putignano, Matteo Vannacci

item.title: On the residual polynilpotence of tree products of groups with locally cyclic edge subgroups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23126v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\mathcal{N}$ be a non-empty class of nilpotent groups closed under taking subgroups, quotient groups, finite direct products, and unrestricted direct powers of the form $\prod_{x \in X}Y_{x}$, where $X \in \mathcal{N}$ and $Y_{x}$ ($x \in X$) are isomorphic copies of a group $Y \in \mathcal{N}$. Let also the symbols $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ and $\mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ denote the class of all torsion-free $\mathcal{N}$-groups and the class of polynilpotent groups such that $X \in \mathit{Poly}_{k}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ if and only if $X$ has a subnormal series of length at most $k$ whose factors belong to $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$. We prove that if all free groups are residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups and $2 \leqslant n < \infty$, then any tree product of $n$ residually $\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$-groups with non-trivial torsion-free locally cyclic edge subgroups is residually a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n+1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group. In particular, all cyclically-pinched one-relator groups are residually finitely generated $(\mathit{Poly}_{3}\overline{\mathcal{N}}\mbox{}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-groups, where $\overline{\mathcal{N}}\mbox{}^{\mathfrak{tf}}$ is the class of all torsion-free nilpotent groups. We prove also that any tree product of $n$ $\mathcal{N}$-groups with non-trivial torsion-free locally cyclic edge subgroups has a homomorphism onto a $(\mathit{Poly}_{n-1}\mathcal{N}^{\mathfrak{tf}})$-group that is injective on all edge subgroups.
item.dc:creator: E. V. Sokolov

item.title: Derivations of Lie $p$-rings with applications on ring extensions and computational methods
item.description: arXiv:2610.23370v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Derivations are a well-known concept in the theory of Lie algebras. Here we investigate them for Lie $p$-rings. We show how they apply in the construction of cyclic extensions and in computational methods; in particular, we demonstrate that a consistency test for Lie $p$-presentations can be facilitated using derivations. The consistency test generalizes inspecific cases to parametrised Lie $p$-presentations and, further, to the construction of Lie $p$-covers. These provide a first building block towards a symbolic Lie $p$-ring generation algorithm.
item.dc:creator: Bettina Eick, Renu Joshi

item.title: Finite power image families and automorphism actions in linear groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.23373v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $k/\mathbb{Q}$ be a finitely generated field extension. We characterize the subgroups $G\leq GL_n(k)$ for which the power images $P_m(G)=\{g^m:g\in G\}$ form a finite family: this holds precisely when $G=N\rtimes F$, where $F$ is finite and $N$ is a uniquely divisible subgroup consisting of unipotent matrices. The subgroup $N$ is canonical and fully invariant.For $e=\exp(G/N)$, we obtain $P_m(G)=P_{\gcd(m,e)}(G)$, exactly $\tau(e)$ distinct power images, and least positive period $e$, where $\tau(e)$ is the number of positive divisors of $e$.Over $\mathbb{Q}$, the group coincides with the full group of rational points of its Zariski closure. Since finite automorphism-orbit count implies finiteness of the power-image family, an affirmative answer to Problem~21.40 of the Kourovka Notebook\cite{Kourovka} follows as a corollary. We further prove that a rational linear group $G$ admits a decomposition $G\cong(\mathbb{Q}^d,+)\rtimes F$, with $d\geq0$ finite and $F$ finite, whenever a virtually nilpotent subgroup of $\operatorname{Aut}(G)$ has finitely many orbits on $G$.The latter argument uses nonconstant invariant rational functions arising from nonzero Lie brackets to obstruct dense orbits. A metabelian action with five orbits on the rational Heisenberg group shows that solubility of the acting group is insufficient.
item.dc:creator: Zhexin Jiang

item.title: Charmenability of twin building lattices
item.description: arXiv:2610.23424v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Let $\Lambda = \mathcal G_A (\mathbb F_q)$ be a minimal simply connected split Kac-Moody group of compact-hyperbolic type, and set $\Gamma=\Lambda/Z(\Lambda)$. We prove that $\Gamma$ is charfinite when $q\geq 11$, or when its Weyl group is $3$-spherical and $q\geq 4$. Here are a few consequences: the only characters of $\Gamma$ are the trivial and regular characters, every invariant random subgroup is supported on $\{e\}$ and $\Gamma$ and these are the only uniformly recurrent subgroups, and every nontrivial unitary $\Gamma$-representation weakly contains the regular representation. Our approach relies on a recent result due to Caprace and Thom, showing that the topological completions $G_+$ and $G_-$ associated to $\Gamma$ have the Howe-Moore property. We prove a criterion of charmenability for irreducible lattices with trivial amenable radical in products of Howe-Moore groups acting geometrically on proper hyperbolic spaces. The criterion requires the visual boundaries to be Poisson boundaries of suitable random walks and the corresponding lattice actions to be essentially free.
item.dc:creator: Cyril Houdayer, Corentin Le Bars

item.title: Subvariety intervals and limit varieties of zero extensions of mirror-word semirings
item.description: arXiv:2610.23478v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: For the mirror word $\mathbf{m}_n=a_1\cdots a_na_n\cdots a_1$, let $\mathcal{V}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n))$ and $\mathcal{W}_n=\mathrm{V}(S(\mathbf{m}_n)^0)$. We show that $[\mathcal{W}_n,\mathcal{W}_{n+1}]$ ($n\geq 1$) and $[\mathcal{V}_n,\mathcal{W}_n]$ ($n\geq 2$) have cardinality $2^{\aleph_0}$. Every variety in $[\mathcal{W}_2,\mathcal{W}_\infty]$ has infinite axiomatic rank. The unique limit subvariety of $\mathcal{W}_1$ is $\mathrm{V}(SR_6)$. For $n\geq 2$, we construct a distinct directed-path limit variety contained in $\mathcal{W}_n$ but not in $\mathcal{V}_n$.
item.dc:creator: Ruijing Wang, Mengya Yue

item.title: Two-generator presentations with a relation gap
item.description: arXiv:2610.23637v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We exhibit two-generator two-relator group presentations that have cyclic relation modules but do not present one-relator groups; this resolves the relation gap problem. By attaching a single 3-cell to each of the corresponding presentation 2-complexes, one obtains counterexamples to Wall's D2 problem.
item.dc:creator: Laurent Bartholdi, Martin R. Bridson, Roman Mikhailov, John Nicholson

item.title: Separable elements and Bruhat orders
item.description: arXiv:2610.22857v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We prove the curious fact that, in any Coxeter group, the intersection of a principal left weak order ideal $[e,x]_L$ with a principal right weak order ideal $[e,y]_R$ has a unique maximal element $\mathrm{lr}(x,y)$ under Bruhat order. We apply this to resolve a conjecture of Hart and Rowley on involutions in weak order ideals. This fact arises from, and is applied to, our study of the theory of separable elements in finite Weyl groups. We use it to prove that for $U=[e,u]_R$ in a Coxeter group $W$, the multiplication map $W/U\times U\rightarrow W$ is surjective, where $W/U$ is the Bj\"{o}rner-Wachs generalized quotient. This resolves and generalizes a conjecture of the authors. For finite Weyl groups, we further prove that this map is bijective if and only if $u$ is separable, thereby classifying the splittings of finite Weyl groups into weak order intervals, and resolving the natural extension of a question of Bj\"orner-Wachs.
item.dc:creator: Christian Gaetz, Yibo Gao

item.title: Signed dual graphs and face spectral gaps of Cayley 2-complexes
item.description: arXiv:2610.22916v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We construct a weighted signed dual multigraph for the Cayley $2$-complex of a finite presentation and represent its $\ell^2$ face Laplacian as a signed graph Laplacian with a diagonal potential. We prove that the face spectral gap above the kernel vanishes for the Baumslag--Solitar groups $\operatorname{BS}(1,m)$, $m\ge2$, using explicit finitely supported face chains. Our main vanishing theorem gives the same conclusion for every finitely presented amenable group with ordinary first Betti number at least two.
item.dc:creator: Bobo Hua, Yong Lin, Tao Wang, Haohang Zhang

item.title: Strongly Choquet-Deny groups and invariant strictly convex renormings
item.description: arXiv:2610.23584v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We introduce and study a strengthening of the notion of Choquet-Deny groups, which we call \emph{strongly Choquet-Deny groups}. We show that a countable group $G$ is strongly Choquet-Deny if and only if for every uniformly bounded representation of $G$ on any separable Banach space $X$, there exists an equivalent $G$-invariant strictly convex norm on $X$. We provide a full classification of finitely generated strongly Choquet-Deny groups and show that a finitely generated group is strongly Choquet-Deny if and only if it is virtually abelian. This fully resolves a question of Mikael de la Salle for finitely generated groups. As a further application, we show that for every uniformly bounded representation of a compact extension of an abelian topological group on any separable Banach space, there exists an equivalent invariant strictly convex norm.
item.dc:creator: Sheldon Dantas, Michal Doucha

item.title: Arithmeticity, superrigidity, and totally geodesic submanifolds of infinite-volume hyperbolic manifolds
item.description: arXiv:2610.23594v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Given an infinite-volume convex cocompact hyperbolic manifold with Fuchsian ends and infinitely many maximal properly immersed totally geodesic submanifolds of dimension at least two intersecting its convex core, we show that it (infinitely) covers an arithmetic hyperbolic manifold. This answers the general version of a question of Oh. As a byproduct of our techniques, we also give a Ratner-type classification of $\mathrm{SO}_0(m,1)$-invariant Radon measures whose support intersects the frame bundle of the interior of the convex core.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Miller

item.title: Some questions related to free-by-cyclic groups and tubular groups
item.description: arXiv:2504.14192v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that a CAT(0) free-by-cyclic tubular group with a single vertex is virtually special, but many of them cannot virtually act freely and cocompactly on CAT(0) cube complexes. This partially confirms a question of Brady--Soroko \cite[Section 9: Question 1]{BS} and answers a question of Lyman \cite[Question 1]{Ly} in the negative. Furthermore, we provide examples of free-by-cyclic groups amalgamated along cyclic subgroups that are not virtually free-by-cyclic. This answers negatively a question of Hagen--Wise \cite[Remark 3.6]{hw}. Lastly, we exhibit an example of a cyclic-subgroup-separable tubular group that does not have the property (VRC) (i.e. every cyclic subgroup is a virtual retract). This answers a question of Minasyan \cite[Question 11.6]{min} in the negative.
item.dc:creator: Xiaolei Wu, Shengkui Ye

item.title: Automorphisms of Twisted Chevalley Groups of type ${}^2 D_\ell \ (\ell \geq 4)$ over Local Rings
item.description: arXiv:2608.02312v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that all automorphisms of twisted Chevalley groups of type ${}^2D_\ell$, $\ell\ge4$, and their elementary subgroups over commutative local rings with $1/2$ are standard. More precisely, for elementary groups, every automorphism is a composition of strictly inner, diagonal, and ring automorphisms; for full groups, a central factor may also occur. In the adjoint case, diagonal automorphisms are strictly inner and the centre is trivial, so only strictly inner and ring factors are needed for both the elementary and full groups.
item.dc:creator: Elena I. Bunina, Deep H. Makadiya

item.title: On the Self-Similarity of Permutational Wreath Products and Their Embedding into Finitely Presented Simple Groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.01868v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: In this work, we study the self-similarity of permutational wreath products of the form \(A \wr_X G\), where \(A\) is a finitely generated abelian group and \(G\) is a self-similar group (the permutational wreath product \(A \wr_X G\) is also known as a lamplighter group). In the case where \(G\) is a non-torsion contracting group, we prove that, under certain conditions, the Scott--R\"over--Nekrashevych group \(V_m(\mathbb{Z}^d \wr_X G)\) is finitely presented and virtually simple. Moreover, we prove that \(\mathbb{Z}^d \wr_X G\) embeds into a finitely presented simple group. Furthermore, this provides a new family of groups that satisfy the Boone--Higman conjecture.
item.dc:creator: Mailton Rego Almeida, Alex Carrazedo Dantas, Altair Santos de Oliveira-Tosti

item.title: Finite quotients of spherical Artin groups
item.description: arXiv:2609.27171v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We show the smallest non-abelian quotients of spherical and affine Artin groups are isomorphic to the smallest non-abelian quotients of the corresponding Coxeter groups. We deduce irreducible spherical Artin groups are determined by their finite quotient groups.
item.dc:creator: Sam Hughes, Thomas Ng, Kaitlin Ragosta, Nancy Scherich, Yvon Verberne

item.title: Maximal subgroups of topological full groups arising from factor maps and subgroupoids
item.description: arXiv:2609.33118v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We construct maximal subgroups of topological full groups and their commutator subgroups using factor maps and wide open subgroupoids of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit spaces, assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness. For two-to-one coverings and prime factor maps with principal target and fibers of cardinality at most two, surjectivity and injectivity of the same induced map on full-group abelianizations characterize maximality of the factor full group and factor commutator subgroup, respectively. For subgroupoids arising from prime-order cyclic actions free on the unit space, the normalizer of the smaller commutator subgroup in the ambient full group is a semidirect product, maximal exactly when the inclusion induces a surjection on full-group abelianizations. In both constructions, the embedded commutator subgroup has a unique maximal overgroup in the ambient commutator subgroup, namely its normalizer. For Cantor minimal systems, the factor construction yields partition stabilizers of the type in the Grigorchuk-Vorobets conjecture. The subgroupoid normalizers act topologically primitively. Groupoid homology makes the criteria computable for these systems and shifts of finite type. Examples include finitely generated nonsimple and locally finite simple maximal subgroups of infinite index in finitely generated infinite simple amenable groups.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matui

item.title: Soficity of One-Relator Groups and Reducible Presentations
item.description: arXiv:2610.02213v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove that every one-relator group is sofic, answering a question of Nate Brown. More generally, every group admitting a reducible presentation without proper powers is sofic, with one proper-power relation allowed at the final reducible step. The proof starts from the endpoint-preserving edge replacements of Poulin--Wr\'obel. We retain the free-group word carried by each terminal replacement and use it to define an \(F(S)\)-valued cocycle repair; in its relative form, the repair preserves the previously chosen generator coordinates while controlling the new relator defect. Coinduction transports the lower cocycle through successive one-relator-product extensions, allowing the construction to be iterated along reducible presentations. For a final relator \(w^m\), cyclic translates of the repaired set amplify a zero-defect set of measure close to \(1/m\) to one of measure close to one. A cocycle criterion then converts arbitrarily small relator defect into finite permutation approximations via a treeable skew-product orbit relation.
item.dc:creator: Jinhyuk Son

item.title: Stabilizers and maximal subgroups of topological full groups
item.description: arXiv:2610.15253v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study closed-set stabilizers in topological full groups of minimal effective ample groupoids with Cantor unit space. For almost finite or purely infinite groupoids, we extend the maximal stabilizer theorem of Grigorchuk and Vorobets to every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup. For a nonempty closed nowhere dense set, maximality of its stabilizer is equivalent to minimality of its stabilizer action, minimality of the regular reduction, and primeness of a canonical wide open subgroupoid. Without assuming almost finiteness or pure infiniteness, we prove spatial rigidity for stabilizers acting minimally on infinite closed nowhere dense sets. Their isomorphism types determine the ambient Kakutani equivalence class and, when Hausdorff, the effective reduction. We also realize every AF groupoid with compact unit space as the full restriction, with its relative topology, of any minimal effective ample groupoid with Cantor unit space to a closed nowhere dense subset. Combining rigidity and realization yields continuum many pairwise nonisomorphic stabilizers in every subgroup containing the commutator subgroup; these stabilizers are maximal when the ambient groupoid is almost finite or purely infinite. The realization also gives explicit AF subquotients of the ambient reduced groupoid $C^*$-algebra, including the CAR algebra, with compatibility on the canonical diagonal subalgebras.
item.dc:creator: Hiroki Matui

item.title: Totally elliptic surface group representations
item.description: arXiv:2411.19748v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A surface group representation into a Lie group is called totally elliptic if every simple closed curve on the surface is mapped to an elliptic element of the target group. In this note, we characterize all totally elliptic surface group representations into $\mathrm{PSL}_2\mathbb{R}$ and $\mathrm{PSL}_2\mathbb{C}$ by showing that they are either representations into a compact subgroup or Deroin--Tholozan representations.
item.dc:creator: Arnaud Maret

item.title: Weak action representability of $2$-nilpotent groups
item.description: arXiv:2604.22578v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In this article, we investigate the representability of actions of the category $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ of $2$-nilpotent groups. We first provide an algebraic characterisation of derived actions in $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ in terms of the group $\operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$ of central automorphisms of an object $X$. We also characterise the morphisms $B \to \operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$ that define an action of $B$ on $X$ in $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$. We then show that $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is not action representable, and that the existence of a weak representation is related to the amalgamation property. We prove that the category $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is weakly action representable, by exhibiting a strong amalgam of a suitable family of abelian subgroups of $\operatorname{Aut}_c(X)$: an explicit weak representing object of $X$ is the abelian group $\operatorname{Hom}(X/[X,X],\operatorname{Z}(X))$. Finally, we show that $\mathsf{Nil}_2(\mathsf{Grp})$ is not locally algebraically cartesian closed.
item.dc:creator: Alessandro Dioguardi Burgio, Manuel Mancini, Tim Van der Linden

item.title: Finite index extensions of treeable equivalence relations are treeable
item.description: arXiv:2610.08986v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We prove that every countable Borel equivalence relation containing a finite index Borel treeable subequivalence relation is Borel treeable. This answers a long-standing question of Jackson--Kechris--Louveau. Our proof is based on a median subalgebra filtration construction on products of trees, together with an extension of the median graph treeing algorithm of Chen--Poulin--Tao--Tserunyan to certain well-behaved increasing unions.
item.dc:creator: Ruiyuan Chen, Anush Tserunyan, Robin Tucker-Drob
